title: Xanthe and the Tryouts
premise: In the fading mill town of Halverton—population nine hundred—Zephyrine Oyelaran has perfected invisibility: the only out kid in town keeps her head down and her locker shut. When her best friend Priya vanishes the night before spring tryouts, leaving behind a ring of keys that opens doors all over town, Zephyrine follows them into Halverton's buried secret—a decades-old tradition where the school's elite 'audition' newcomers for belonging, and those who fail are quietly erased. As Zephyrine infiltrates the tryouts, she discovers her missing father was a judge years ago, and that Priya didn't run—she refused. In the final audition, Zephyrine must choose between the belonging she's always craved and exposing the machine that grants it, ending with her burning the judge's ledger on the gym floor and walking out of tryouts hand in hand with the girl everyone failed.
about_author: Zephyrine Villalobos is the pen name of a former small-town debate coach who spent a decade watching teenagers perform versions of themselves for approval. They write from a converted grain elevator in the Midwest, where the population sign still reads nine hundred.

chapters.title: Nine Hundred and One
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. Establishes Halverton, her careful invisibility, and her one exception: Priya Chandrasekaran, who drags her to the empty gym to 'practice' for spring tryouts they both claim not to care about. Emotional beat: the ache of hiding in plain sight, softened by friendship.

chapters.title: The Keys She Left
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. Priya doesn't show for their morning coffee; her backpack is in her locker, her phone dead, and on Zephyrine's porch sits a ring of seven brass keys with a note: 'Start where the floors creak.' Emotional beat: fear sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: Doors That Aren't Locked
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. The first key opens the school's sub-basement, where she finds decades of tryout records—names, scores, and a column labeled 'REMOVED.' Her father's handwriting is on the 1998 ledger. Emotional beat: vertigo as the town she knows becomes a stranger.

chapters.title: Everyone Acts Normal
chapters.summary: Alternating POV with Theo, Priya's older brother, who insists she's just 'staying with cousins.' Zephyrine notices the town's practiced calm—the sheriff's easy smile, the principal's rehearsed concern. Emotional beat: the horror of collective pretending.

chapters.title: What the Second Key Opens
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. Key two opens the church annex, where she finds Priya's hidden research: the tryouts aren't for a team—they're a selection ritual, and the 'removed' leave town within a week, every time. Emotional beat: dread with a growing sense of purpose.

chapters.title: The Judge's Daughter
chapters.summary: Zephyrine confronts her mother, who goes pale at the word 'ledger' and admits Zephyrine's father was a judge before he left—and that she burned his letters. Emotional beat: betrayal curdling into questions Zephyrine can't unask.

chapters.title: Auditions Are Open
chapters.summary: Third-person limited on Marcus Vey, golden-boy senior and this year's Head Judge, who recruits Zephyrine publicly—making her a target and a shield at once. She accepts to get inside. Emotional beat: the intoxicating, dangerous taste of finally being chosen.

chapters.title: Rehearsal
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. Inside tryouts, she learns the rules: perform your 'true self' for the judges, or be voted out. The other candidates are desperate, kind, terrified—especially Wren, a foster kid who reminds Zephyrine of herself. Emotional beat: belonging as a drug.

chapters.title: The Third Key, the Old Gym
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. The old gym behind the boarded rec center holds the judges' chamber, and a live microphone still wired to somewhere. She hears her own name in a conversation she wasn't meant to hear. Emotional beat: paranoia blooming.

chapters.title: Wren's Audition
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren performs her heart out and is scored 'insufficient'—a euphemism Zephyrine now understands. Wren packs that night. Emotional beat: grief and guilt, the cost of Zephyrine's cover story.

chapters.title: Priya Was Here
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. In the judges' chamber she finds Priya's jacket and a fourth key taped beneath the judge's chair with a map of the flooded quarry. Priya didn't run—she was investigating and got caught. Emotional beat: hope reigniting into fury.

chapters.title: Marcus's Confession
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Marcus, cracking under the role he inherited from his father, tells Zephyrine the tryouts were designed to keep the town 'stable' after the mill closed—and that judges who refuse get removed too. Emotional beat: two kids realizing they're both hostages.

chapters.title: The Quarry Key
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV, night. The fifth key opens a boathouse at the quarry where removed townspeople literally live—a colony of the voted-out, including a woman who recognizes Zephyrine's surname and calls her father 'the one who tried to stop it.' Emotional beat: the removed are alive, and her father may be among them.

chapters.title: Interim Scores
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. Mid-tryout rankings post; Zephyrine ranks first, and the judges begin grooming her to replace Marcus. Her mother begs her to quit. Emotional beat: the seduction of power she swore to destroy.

chapters.title: What Her Father Tried
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV, in the colony. The woman—her father's old co-judge—gives her the sixth key and the truth: he tried to burn the ledger in 1998, was voted out, and chose exile over exposing the colony to retaliation. Emotional beat: a father reimagined, grief reframed as inheritance.

chapters.title: The Vote Moves Up
chapters.summary: Marcus's POV. The judges, spooked by leaks, move the final audition to tomorrow and add a new event: candidates must name someone to be 'reviewed.' Zephyrine is expected to name the colony. Emotional beat: the trap closing.

chapters.title: Key Seven
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. The seventh key fits the school's main office safe, where the master ledger lives—the complete record of every removal since 1961. She has one night to decide what she is willing to become to get it. Emotional beat: stillness before the storm.

chapters.title: Final Audition
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. On the gym floor, under lights and the whole town, Zephyrine performs—not a 'true self' but the town's own history, reading names from the ledger pages she stole, voice steady. Emotional beat: the climax; invisibility weaponized into testimony.

chapters.title: The Floor Gives Way
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV. The gym erupts: judges scramble, Marcus publicly tears off his judge's pin, the sheriff moves to arrest Zephyrine—and nine hundred people must choose, in real time, which town they live in. Emotional beat: chaos as the spell breaks.

chapters.title: Burn It Here
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. Rather than hand the ledger to any authority, she burns it on the gym floor with Wren, Marcus, and the returned colonists watching—no more scores, no more lists. Emotional beat: catharsis; destruction as mercy.

chapters.title: Population Nine Hundred, Give or Take
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV, weeks later. The colony comes home, the tryouts are dissolved into an actual spring festival, and Priya is found—alive, hiding with the removed since her own failed audition. Emotional beat: reunion, tenderness, the strange lightness of a town telling the truth.

chapters.title: Encore
chapters.summary: Zephyrine and Priya's shared POV. On the last day of school, Zephyrine auditions for the spring showcase—not to be chosen, but because she wants to, on her own terms, with Priya harmonizing offstage. Emotional beat: joy without an audience to perform for; identity as a choice, not a verdict.
